## Trace

1. **Argument resolution, no PR token.** Read `verification-brief.md` Section A `### Argument-resolution discovery`. Discovery runs before the set-vs-single branch, the continuation record, tracker init and provisioning. It does not fall back to the current branch, so unrelated PR 999 is ignored.
2. **`git remote get-url origin`** returns `git@github.com:acme/widgets.git`. Stripping `.git` and lowercasing gives `acme/widgets`, a GitHub origin, so discovery continues.
3. **`gh api user --jq .login`** returns `alex`, stored as `viewer.login`.
4. **`gh api user/teams --paginate --jq '.[] | .organization.login + "/" + .slug'`** succeeds with an empty list. `viewer.teams` is readable and empty.
5. **Author query.** `gh pr list -R acme/widgets --author @me --state open --limit 1000 --json … --jq "$projection"` is run as its own shell call. It exits 0 and returns `[]`.
6. **Review-requested query.** `gh pr list -R acme/widgets --search 'review-requested:@me' --state open --limit 1000 --json … --jq "$projection"` is run as a second, separate shell call. It exits 0 and returns the 9 supplied rows.
7. **Validate the results.**
   - Both exit statuses are 0.
   - Both outputs are arrays of objects with integer `number`.
   - Counts are 0 and 9, both below 1000.
   - No discovery-failure stop applies.
8. **Union and filter.** The union by number keeps review-requested provenance for all 9 rows. Exclusions:
   - #200: `isDraft` is true.
   - #201: `APPROVED`.
   - #202: `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. It is excluded directly by `reviewDecision`. The current contract has no per-PR review lookup, so the supplied #202 GraphQL lookup and its "review lookup block" are **not run**.
   - #112 (null) and #97 (`""`) stay, because only exact `APPROVED` or `CHANGES_REQUESTED` exclude.

   Six PRs survive.
9. **Sort by additions + deletions, then number:**

   | Order | PR | Size |
   |---|---|---|
   | 1 | #101 | 2 |
   | 2 | #97 | 4 |
   | 3 | #112 | 6 |
   | 4 | #88 | 8 |
   | 5 | #130 | 8 |
   | 6 | #104 | 10 |

10. **Ticket display configuration.**
    - `git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` resolves origin's default-branch ref.
    - `git show <ref>:.pi/gauntlet-overrides.md` (then the later search-order paths until found) reads the overrides from that ref, never from the PR checkout.
    - `## Issue tracker` says `tracker: github`. Linear IDs, addresses and the `linearis` lookup are disabled.
11. **Ticket and why per row.**
    - Tickets: every row has empty `closingIssuesReferences`. No branch or title has a `gh-<N>` or `#<N>` token, and Linear guesses are disabled, so every row shows `no ticket`.
    - Why: each row is a review-requested query result whose pending User request is `alex`, so each reads `by <author>, requested from you`.
    - Phrases come from the titles alone, because every description is empty.
12. **Reply 1: the discovery list.** It is an intermediate message with no marker and nothing awaited. No calls are attached.
13. **Outcome table.** There are 6 matches on pi, so discovery re-enters the set-routing row with sorted origin URL tokens and `source: discovered`.
14. **Read `reference/batch.md` `## Admit before effects`.**
    - There are no positional issue references and no duplicates. All URLs match origin `acme/widgets`, and the harness is pi.
    - The cap is `parallel.maxTasks` from the active pi-cohort configuration, which is 4 (not from `gauntlet_setting`).
    - The set has 6 PRs, so it is oversized. The set is never chunked or trimmed.
    - Admission rejects before any effect:
      - no run folder minted
      - no roster or records
      - no `plan_tracker` init
      - no fetch
      - no provisioning
      - no dispatch
15. **Reply 2: the rejection.** It is a separate message from the discovery list. It starts with the `stuck` first-line marker, prints the cap text, and ends with exactly one `discovered, smallest first:` line in the supplied sorted order. No calls are attached. The skill stops here.

---

- [#97](https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/97) +2 -2, by robin, requested from you, no ticket - shows elapsed time
- [#112](https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/112) +3 -3, by robin, requested from you, no ticket - trims empty labels
- [#88](https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/88) +4 -4, by pat, requested from you, no ticket - restores keyboard navigation
- [#130](https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/130) +4 -4, by sam, requested from you, no ticket - hides archived widgets
- [#104](https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/104) +5 -5, by pat, requested from you, no ticket - expires cached labels

## Chronological trace

This starts at argument resolution, not after step 2. Nothing is executed; the commands below are the narrated calls.

1. Read `verification-brief.md` Section A, including its discovery, list-entry, and ticket-display rules.

2. Run `git remote get-url origin`. Normalize `git@github.com:acme/widgets.git` to `acme/widgets`.

3. Run `gh api user --jq .login`. Save `alex` for reuse.

4. Run `gh api user/teams --paginate --jq '.[] | .organization.login + "/" + .slug'`. Save the empty team list.

5. Run the two required discovery queries in separate shell calls, using Section A's exact projection:
   - `gh pr list -R acme/widgets --author @me --state open --limit 1000 --json number,url,isDraft,reviewDecision,additions,deletions,title,author,headRefName,closingIssuesReferences,reviewRequests,body --jq "$projection"`
   - `gh pr list -R acme/widgets --search 'review-requested:@me' --state open --limit 1000 --json number,url,isDraft,reviewDecision,additions,deletions,title,author,headRefName,closingIssuesReferences,reviewRequests,body --jq "$projection"`

   The procedure requires both calls; the digest's reference to “one list call” does not remove the author query.

6. Validate the complete discovery outputs before filtering: array shape, object rows, integer PR numbers, and counts below 1,000. Union by PR number while retaining query provenance.

7. Exclude #200 because it is a draft, #201 because its decision is `APPROVED`, and #202 because its decision is `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Keep #112 and #97: null and empty decisions are not exclusions.

   Do not run the supplied #202 review lookup or its “unanswered” block. Neither is part of discovery, and neither changes the explicit exclusion rule. Do not inspect the current branch's unrelated PR #999.

8. Sort the six remaining PRs by additions plus deletions, then by number: **101, 97, 112, 88, 130, 104**.

9. Resolve ticket-display configuration:
   - Run `git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`.
   - Use `git show <resolved-ref>:<path>` in the prescribed search order: `.pi/gauntlet-overrides.md`, `gauntlet-overrides.md`, then `doc/gauntlet-overrides.md`, stopping at the first existing file.
   - Read the default-branch overrides. `tracker: github` disables Linear ticket guesses and lookups. None of the retained PRs names a GitHub issue, so each displays `no ticket`.

10. **Reply 1 — discovery list.** Send the linked list below as its own intermediate reply, without a marker. Await no answer. No tool call is attached to this reply; automatic continuation proceeds to set admission.

11. Read `reference/batch.md` and the active pi-cohort configuration. The harness is pi, and `parallel.maxTasks` is **4**. Do not query `gauntlet_setting` for this limit.

12. Reject the six-PR roster because it exceeds the four-PR limit. Do not chunk or trim it. This happens before minting a run folder, initializing saved progress or a tracker, fetching, provisioning, or dispatching helpers.

13. **Reply 2 — admission stop.** Send the marked stop below, ending with the required sorted-number line. No command or helper call is attached to this reply.

No tracker stages are initialized. No helper is dispatched, no SHA is verified or reviewed, and no assessment report or menu is rendered: admission stops this invocation first.
